items.content:
# Project: Building a Number Guessing Game

In this capstone project for Unit 6, you will combine all core repetition and control flow skills to build an interactive **Number Guessing Game**.

### Core Architecture
Every guessing game operates in a continuous control loop:
```
+-----------------------+
|  Initialize Secret    |  (e.g. secret = 42, attempts = 5)
+-----------------------+
           |
           v
+-----------------------+ <---------------+
| Prompt Player Guess   |                 |
+-----------------------+                 |
           |                              |
           v                              |
+-----------------------+                 |
| Validate Range        | -- [Invalid] ---+ (use continue)
+-----------------------+
           |
      [Valid Number]
           v
+-----------------------+
| Check Guess vs Secret |
+-----------------------+
    |         |        \
    | Too Low | Too High\ Match!
    v         v          v
Print Hint Print Hint  Print "Winner!" & break
    |         |
    +----+----+
         |
         v
  Decrement Attempts
         |
    Attempts Left?
    /            \
  [Yes]          [No]
    |              |
 (Repeat)     Print "Game Over" & break
```

### Testing & Determinism
In automated testing, user inputs are scripted as newline-separated strings (e.g. `"50\n75\n68"`). Each `input()` call consumes the next scripted line in sequence, ensuring completely deterministic and reproducible execution.

items.prompt: Why is a `while` loop or `while True` loop preferred over a fixed `for` loop when building an open-ended guessing game where the player has unlimited attempts?

Because `while` loops run 10 times faster in Python

items.explanation: When the number of repetitions is unknown beforehand and depends on a dynamic condition (like whether the guess matches the secret), an indefinite `while` loop is the natural choice.

items.prompt: What runtime error will occur when executing this guessing game snippet?
items.buggy_code:
secret = 50
guess = input("Enter your guess: ")
if guess < secret:
    print("Too low")
options: TypeError: `<` not supported between instances of `str` and `int`
ValueError: secret must be a string
items.correct_answer: TypeError: `<` not supported between instances of `str` and `int`
items.fixed_code:
secret = 50
guess = int(input("Enter your guess: "))
if guess < secret:
    print("Too low")
items.explanation: `input()` returns a string. Comparing a string to an integer with `<` or `>` raises a TypeError. You must convert with `int(input())`.

items.prompt: Why does this attempt-limited game loop freeze indefinitely?
items.buggy_code:
secret = 25
attempts = 3
while attempts > 0:
    guess = int(input())
    if guess == secret:
        print("Won")
        break
    print("Try again")
options: `attempts` is never decremented (`attempts -= 1` is missing), creating an infinite loop
The guess should not be converted to int
items.correct_answer: `attempts` is never decremented (`attempts -= 1` is missing), creating an infinite loop
items.fixed_code:
secret = 25
attempts = 3
while attempts > 0:
    guess = int(input())
    if guess == secret:
        print("Won")
        break
    print("Try again")
    attempts -= 1
items.explanation: Because `attempts` remains 3 forever, the loop condition `attempts > 0` never becomes False on incorrect guesses, causing an infinite loop.

items.title: Challenge: Complete Guessing Game Capstone
items.prompt:
Build the complete Number Guessing Game engine:
- `secret = 64`, maximum allowed attempts = 3.
- In each round, read an integer `guess = int(input())`.
- If `guess < 1 or guess > 100`: print `"Invalid guess"` and `continue` (do NOT consume an attempt!).
- Consume an attempt: increment attempts counter.
- If `guess == secret`: print `f"Congratulations! Guessed in {attempts} attempts!"` and `break`.
- Else if `guess < secret`: print `"Too low"`.
- Else: print `"Too high"`.
- If the player uses all 3 attempts without winning: print `"Game over! The number was 64."`
items.starter_code:
secret = 64
max_attempts = 3
attempts = 0
won = False

# Build complete game loop with input guard, hint system, and attempt cap
items.explanation: This capstone integrates: input range guard using `continue` without incrementing attempts, directional hints ("Too low" / "Too high"), attempt counting up to max_attempts, early `break` on victory, and game-over fallback.
